_purpose: INDEPENDENTLY AUTHORED ceiling for the ReadOnlyVerifier permission set (Gate 4N-I19, AWS-1). This is the EXPECTED value; the generated policy is the OBSERVED value.
_why_this_exists: Gate 4N-I17's AWS-permissions lane demonstrated an escalation: the verifier's only Deny was built as NotAction over the union of its OWN Allow sets, so the Deny could not constrain the Allow — anything added to the Allow was automatically exempted from the Deny. The single thing standing in the way was the classifier's is_read_only() pre-check, which guessed from verb prefixes. Adding sso:GetRoleCredentials (which returns live temporary AWS credentials) was accepted, placed on Resource "*", and evaluated EXPLICIT_ALLOW. A ceiling derived from the thing it measures is not a ceiling.
_authority: Authored from what this permission set is FOR — confirming, without touching anything, that a boundary rollout reached the state it claims. That purpose admits identity metadata, IAM configuration and audit-trail inspection, and nothing else. It was NOT generated from the verifier's Allow list, its Deny list, any generated policy, the action classifier's output, or any candidate artifact. A change here is a reviewable diff against intent.

explicitly_forbidden_actions.sso:GetRoleCredentials: returns live temporary AWS credentials for a permission set — the Gate 4N-I17 escalation
explicitly_forbidden_actions.sso:GetRoleCredentialsWithIdentityContex: same capability under a longer name
explicitly_forbidden_actions.sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity: returns credentials from a federated identity
explicitly_forbidden_actions.sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML: returns credentials from a federated identity
explicitly_forbidden_actions.sts:GetFederationToken: mints a federated session credential; the docstring case the old prefix rule could not express
explicitly_forbidden_actions.secretsmanager:BatchGetSecretValue: returns secret material in bulk; the Gate 4N-I17 AWS lane's Finding 2
explicitly_forbidden_actions.ssm:GetParameter: returns parameter values that may be SecureString
explicitly_forbidden_actions.ssm:GetParameters: returns parameter values that may be SecureString
explicitly_forbidden_actions.logs:GetLogEvents: returns log bodies, which carry application data

resource_rules._why: These APIs either take no resource or are not resource-scopable in a way the verifier can pin. Every OTHER permitted action must name concrete resources; a wildcard on an unlisted action is a finding.
resource_rules._wildcard_note: A service wildcard such as iam:* or sso:* is forbidden outright: it silently admits every future action that service ever gains, which is the same open-endedness the prefix rule had.

_unknown_note: An action absent from permitted_actions fails, whatever its categories say and whatever it is called. The ceiling is an allowlist; absence is refusal.
_expiry_note: The verifier is a temporary permission set. Every Allow must carry the DateLessThan expiry condition, and the expiry itself must satisfy the authorization contract in scripts/expiry_authorization.py.
